nodes.name: Wet Chemical Displacement
nodes.procedure: The Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ catalyst is synthesized on nickel foam (NF) using a wet chemical displacement strategy. Specifically, the spontaneous redox reaction between Ru³⁺ and Ni accelerates the corrosion of the metal matrix due to the favorable thermodynamic process and the assistance of soluble Cl⁻. Meanwhile, Ni²⁺ ions coordinate with OH⁻ to form low-crystalline nickel hydroxide (LC-Ni(OH)₂). As a result, Ru single atoms are uniformly dispersed on LC-Ni(OH)₂ to obtain Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheet catalyst.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ru single-atom catalyst supported on high-crystalline nickel hydroxide support (Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂) is prepared by hydrothermal method.
nodes.source_text: Ru single-atom catalyst supported on high-crystalline nickel hydroxide support (Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂) is prepared by hydrothermal method (Figure 1a).

nodes.description: HER LSV polarization curves in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ catalyst exhibits... only 9 mV overpotential at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... requires only 102 and 136 mV overpotential to achieve current densities of 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻²... the Tafel slope of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ is smaller than that of Pt/C... The exchange current density of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂... is significantly higher than that of Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.description: HER performance metrics in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: Compared with Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ (0.12 s⁻¹), the Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ (16.12 s⁻¹) catalyst with an ideal electronic structure exhibits a larger TOF at 70 mV.

nodes.description: AEM electrolyzer performance in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂||FeNi LDH-based AEM electrolyzer only requires a voltage of 1.69 V to reach 1.0 A cm⁻² in 1.0 M KOH... can continue to operate stably in 1.0 M KOH... for at least 500 hours at 500 mA cm⁻².

nodes.description: AEM electrolyzer performance in 1.0 M KOH seawater
nodes.source_text: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂||FeNi LDH exhibits good ability to generate a current density of 1.0 A cm⁻² at 1.77 V in a 1.0 M KOH seawater electrolyzer... can continue to operate stably in 1.0 M KOH seawater for at least 500 hours at 500 mA cm⁻².

nodes.description: HER chronopotentiometry stability tests at multiple current densities
nodes.source_text: The Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ catalyst can operate continuously for 500, 300, and 50 h at 10, 500, and 1000 mA cm⁻², respectively (Figure 3g).

nodes.description: Mass activity comparison at specific overpotentials
nodes.source_text: the mass activity of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ is 4.22 and 10.70 times that of Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ at 10 and 50 mV, respectively

nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscope (SEM) image in Figure 1b indicates that Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ exhibits a highly open 3D network structure compared to Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ (Figure 1d)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows random distribution of order and disorder lattice fringes with interplanar distance of 0.270 nm corresponding to (100) crystal plane of Ni(OH)₂; Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ shows high-quality lattice fringes assigned to (100) crystal plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Remarkably, the lattice fringes present a random distribution of order and disorder in the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ (Figure 1c)... the interplanar distance of 0.270 nm corresponds to the (100) crystal plane of Ni(OH)₂

nodes.characterization_summary: Bright atomic columns identified as isolated Ru single atoms on low crystalline support in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ without Ru nanoparticles; Ru atoms regularly located at ordered lattice points in Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bright atomic columns isolated on the low crystalline support can be distinguished as Ru single atoms in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂, without the obvious appearance of Ru nanoparticles (Figure 1f and 1g)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru, Ni, and O elements are uniformly dispersed in both catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis, Ru, Ni, and O elements are uniformly dispersed in the catalyst (Figure S3 and Table S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: High-quality lattice fringes in Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ consistent with XRD results (Figure S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-quality lattice fringes in Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ are also assigned to the (100) crystal plane, consistent with the X-ray diffraction (XRD) results (Figure S1)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂: Ni 2p binding energy shifts to higher value, Ru 3p peaks at 461.62 eV (3p₃/₂) and 481.74 eV (3p₁/₂) show negative shift vs Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ indicating increased Ru electron density; O 1s shows oxygen vacancy peak at 531.38 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is noticeable that the Ni 2p binding energy of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shifts to a higher value than that of Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂. On the contrary, the Ru 3p peak of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ exhibits a negative shift compared to Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂... the significant oxygen vacancy peak at 531.38 eV in the O 1s spectrum

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows strong signal peak indicating unsaturated coordination of metallic Ni sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The strong signal peak of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ also indicates the unsaturated coordination of metallic Ni sites in electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) (Figure S5)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows Ni K-edge XANES shift to positive energy and higher white line intensity vs Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂; Ru K-edge indicates lower oxidation state (+0.46) close to Ru foil; Ni K-edge EXAFS: Ni-O coordination number 5.3 (vs 5.9 in Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂); Ru K-edge EXAFS: no Ru-Ru bond, shorter Ru-Ni bond length.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the normalized X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES), the Ni K-edge spectra of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shift to positive energy relative to Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂... The Ru single-atoms (+0.46) in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ have a metal-like electronic structure... the coordination number of Ni-O decreases from 5.9 (Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂) to 5.3 (Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-H* intermediate at 1901 cm⁻¹ observed for both catalysts, stronger intensity for Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂; H₃O⁺ signal at 1750 cm⁻¹ only in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂; HBWn peak at 3000 cm⁻¹ increases with voltage in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ indicating local acidic microenvironment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the application of voltage, the formation of Ru-H* intermediate can be observed at 1901 cm⁻¹ for Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ and Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ catalysts... a significant hydronium (H₃O⁺) signal can be detected at 1750 cm⁻¹ in Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows H₃O⁺ absorption band at 3525 cm⁻¹ indicating formation of large number of H₃O⁺ species during HER, significantly different from Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4e, an obvious absorption band is observed for Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ at the vibration frequency of 3525 cm⁻¹ corresponding to the bending of the O-H groups in H₃O⁺

nodes.characterization_summary: Only trace dissolution of Ru atoms from Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ during stability test at 10 and 500 mA cm⁻² for 200 h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) shows only trace dissolution of Ru atoms during the stability test at 10 and 500 mA cm⁻² for 200 h (Figure 3h)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ shows contact angle of 6.21° indicating superhydrophilic surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The contact angle of Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ is 6.21°, implying that the superhydrophilic Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ self-supporting electrode accelerates the mass transfer efficiency

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ and Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ show similar electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) values indicating comparable ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the measurement of Cdl, Ru-LC-Ni(OH)₂ and Ru-HC-Ni(OH)₂ catalysts present similar electrochemical surface area (ECSA) (Figure S21-S23 and Table S6)
